page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance sits in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently place the instance in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth also shows constraints, with uncached large-block reads registering at 21.24 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput are relatively low, with Redis SET operations achieving 2.86 million operations per second and web serving throughput reaching 2.44 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest performance profile, the ecs.sn2.large offers an entry-level option for workloads that require dedicated resources without high-performance demands. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, basic web serving, development environments, and lightweight database tasks that do not require high I/O or intensive computational power.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, this instance utilizes the KVM hypervisor and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its CPU and memory performance in the lower tiers, with weak single-core and multi-core results, and a static web serving throughput of 2.44 GB/sec. Given these performance characteristics, the ecs.sn2.large is best utilized for lightweight, non-intensive workloads such as development environments, basic web serving, and low-traffic database operations where dedicated CPU resources are required but high computational throughput is not critical.
